compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

observations.body: Jesus contrasts the good shepherd with a hired hand, says he lays down his life for the sheep, and speaks of authority to lay it down and take it again.
observations.label: The good shepherd lays down his life

observations.body: The passage presents shepherd identity, danger, known sheep, one flock, chosen self-giving, and received command as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: shepherd identity, danger, known sheep, one flock, chosen self-giving, and received command

observations.body: The passage places self giving shepherd beside shepherd identity, danger, known sheep, one flock, chosen self-giving, and received command.
observations.label: self giving shepherd

payload.posture: Read John 10:11–18 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the saying uses shepherd and flock relations rather than altar procedure
payload.title: The good shepherd lays down his life
